passage:
"Should I ask Gurleen about the weekend?" Pema whispered to Tashi at the pantry window.
"Look first," said Tashi.
Pema looked. Gurleen was walking fast towards the lift with earphones in and a laptop bag hugged to the chest, eyes on the floor.
"Earphones and a hurry," said Pema. "Not a good moment."
"You could still call out."
"I'd get a half-smile and a nod. I'll wait." Ten minutes later, Gurleen came back to the pantry, pulled out one earphone and reached for the kettle.
"Hey," said Pema. "How was the wedding trip?"
Gurleen's whole face opened. "Oh, it was a disaster and I loved it. Do you have time?"

qa.q: What was Gurleen wearing when walking towards the lift?
qa.a: Earphones, with a laptop bag hugged to the chest.

qa.q: How did Pema feel on seeing Gurleen's earphones and quick walk?
qa.a: Hesitant, sensing it was not a good moment to start a chat, so Pema decided to wait.

qa.q: What did Pema do that gave the chat a better chance?
qa.a: Pema held off while Gurleen was hurrying, then greeted Gurleen when one earphone came out at the pantry.

qa.q: How might Gurleen have felt if Pema had called out in the corridor?
qa.a: Possibly interrupted or hurried, and likely to give only a half-smile and a nod; in the pantry Gurleen's whole face opened.

grounding: A person reads earphones, hurry and a turned-away face as a sign not to start a chat, waits, and gets a warm reply.

passage: My name is Bhupen. On the evening train home there is a woman from my building, Jyoti, whom I like talking to. Last Tuesday she was sitting by the window with her earphones in, forehead resting against the glass, bag on the lap like a shield. I had a joke ready about the lift being broken again. I looked at her posture, the way she turned her whole body away from the aisle, and I kept the joke to myself. I read my book instead. At our stop she took out the earphones, saw me and said, "Sorry, long day." I said, "No problem. The lift's broken again, by the way." She laughed properly.

qa.q: Where did Bhupen see Jyoti last Tuesday?
qa.a: On the evening train home, sitting by the window.

qa.q: What was Bhupen thinking when looking at Jyoti's posture?
qa.a: That Jyoti might want to be left alone right now, since the body was turned away and the earphones were in.

qa.q: What did Bhupen choose to do with the joke, and what happened?
qa.a: Bhupen held it back and read a book, then shared it at the stop when Jyoti removed the earphones, and Jyoti laughed.

qa.q: What might Jyoti have been feeling on the train?
qa.a: Tired after a long day and in need of quiet. Jyoti said sorry for the long day, which suggests the silence was not about Bhupen.

grounding: A person notices earphones and a turned-away posture and holds off starting a chat, then gets a warm reply later.

passage:
Mentor's note, new-joiner programme, Friday.
Vaibhav has been keen to meet people on other teams. This morning he wanted to ask Madhav from finance about the budget tool. I saw him walk toward Madhav's desk, then stop. Madhav had his earphones in, was typing fast, and had two coffee cups beside him, clearly racing a deadline. Vaibhav turned back and sat down.
At lunch, Madhav was sitting alone, earphones off, stretching. Vaibhav went over. "Hi, I'm Vaibhav, new in operations. Do you have five minutes sometime about the budget tool?" Madhav smiled. "Sit, I've got ten now. This morning was madness." They talked for twenty minutes.
Afterwards I mentioned to Vaibhav that waiting was a good call. He said he didn't want to be the person who interrupts.

qa.q: What did Madhav have beside him at his desk?
qa.a: Two coffee cups.

qa.q: What was Vaibhav feeling when he stopped near Madhav's desk?
qa.a: He was hesitant and considerate, sensing from the earphones and fast typing that Madhav was under pressure, and didn't want to intrude.

qa.q: Why did waiting until lunch work better?
qa.a: Madhav was relaxed and free, so he welcomed the question warmly and even gave more time than asked.

qa.q: How might Madhav have reacted if Vaibhav had interrupted in the morning?
qa.a: He might have felt annoyed or rushed and given a short answer, making a worse first impression.

grounding: Shows a person noticing cues that someone is busy and holding off on starting a chat, which leads to a warmer reply later.

passage:
Tuesday night.
I've been meaning to ask Kishore from 4B about the society meeting on water tanks. Today I saw him at the gate. He was on the phone, frowning, carrying three bags of groceries, walking fast. I almost said "Hi, one quick thing." Then I noticed he didn't even look up. So I just nodded and let him pass.
Tomorrow, I thought.
This evening I saw him again on the bench outside, feeding the cats, relaxed. I sat down and asked about the meeting. He laughed. "Thank god you didn't catch me this morning. My mother's flight was delayed and I was going mad." He told me everything about the tanks and even offered to come with me to the next meeting.
Glad I waited.
Kiran

qa.q: What was Kishore carrying at the gate?
qa.a: Three bags of groceries.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel on deciding to let Kishore pass?
qa.a: Kiran felt a little hesitant but considerate, sensing from his frown and hurry that it wasn't the right moment.

qa.q: What did Kiran's choice to wait lead to?
qa.a: A relaxed, warm conversation in the evening where Kishore shared everything and offered to come to the next meeting.

qa.q: How was Kishore feeling that morning?
qa.a: He was stressed and distracted because his mother's flight was delayed.

grounding: Shows a person reading cues that a neighbour is hurried and turned away, holding off, and getting a warm reply later.

passage:
Dilnaz: hey! I saw you on the metro this morning 🙂
Shankar: oh no, really? I didn't see you
Dilnaz: yeah you had your earphones in and your eyes closed. looked like you needed it, so I didn't say hi
Shankar: honestly thank you. I'd been up all night finishing a presentation
Shankar: I'd have been a zombie
Dilnaz: haha I figured. how did it go?
Shankar: went well actually! the client liked it
Dilnaz: amazing 🎉
Shankar: let's get coffee this week, I'll be human by then
Dilnaz: deal. Thursday?
Shankar: Thursday 👍

qa.q: What was Shankar doing on the metro?
qa.a: Shankar had earphones in and eyes closed.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz thinking when deciding not to say hi?
qa.a: Dilnaz felt considerate and a bit protective, sensing Shankar needed rest.

qa.q: How did Dilnaz's choice help their friendship?
qa.a: By not intruding, Dilnaz got a grateful, warm reply later and a plan for coffee.

qa.q: How did Shankar feel about not being disturbed?
qa.a: Shankar felt grateful and relieved, having been up all night and ready to be a zombie.

grounding: Shows a person noticing someone with earphones and eyes closed and holding off, which leads to a warmer reply later.

passage: On the 7:40 bus from Nandurbar, Vijay spotted Madhuri three seats ahead. They had been in the same class till tenth, and he hadn't seen her in six years. He half stood, then noticed: earphones in, eyes closed, forehead against the window, a thick file clutched on her lap. Her lips were moving as if she were going over something. An exam, maybe, or an interview. He sat back down. For forty minutes he watched the cotton fields go by and let her be. At the kasba stop she pulled out the earphones, stretched and looked around. That was his moment. "Madhuri? Vijay, from Sharda Vidyalaya." Her face opened into a grin. "Vijay! I just finished revising for my interview. Walk with me to the office?"

qa.q: What was Madhuri holding on her lap?
qa.a: She was holding a thick file.

qa.q: Why did Vijay sit back down instead of greeting Madhuri?
qa.a: He felt eager to say hello but hesitant to intrude, since her earphones, closed eyes and moving lips suggested she was busy revising.

qa.q: When was the right moment to start the chat, and why?
qa.a: At the kasba stop, when she took out her earphones and looked around, because she was now open to talk.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have felt if Vijay had interrupted her on the bus?
qa.a: She might have felt distracted and a bit annoyed before her interview, and the reunion would have been less warm.

grounding: Shows someone noticing another person's earphones and focus, holding off on a chat until she is open, and getting a warm reply.
